chunks: My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from ‘Ali ibn Nu’mān, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muskān, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Verily, Allāh, the Blessed and the Exalted, manifests (His Mercy) to the Zuwwār of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) before He does (so) to the people who are in ‘Arafāt. He fulfils their needs, forgives their sins, and accepts their intercession for their requests, and thereafter He attends to the people in ‘Arafāt and honours them in the same way.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husain's grave on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes a comparative hierarchy of divine manifestation, placing the visitors of Imam al-Husain (a.s.) above the pilgrims of ‘Arafah, who are traditionally considered the most favored group on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the concept of *tajalli* (divine self-disclosure) specifically linked to the Ahl al-Bayt, suggesting that their intercession (*shafa'ah*) and the spiritual status of their devotees hold precedence in the cosmic order of mercy.

He fulfils their needs, forgives their sins, and accepts their intercession for their requests, and thereafter He attends to the people in ‘Arafāt and honours them in the same way.
